::: {#exm-training-step}

#### One step of the soft rule

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
one_rule = SoftRule()
one_optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(one_rule.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
grad_at_start = one_rule.cutoff.grad
one_optimizer.zero_grad()
one_loss = nn.functional.binary_cross_entropy(one_rule(ink_01), is_one)
one_loss.backward()
grad_after_backward = one_rule.cutoff.grad.item()
one_optimizer.step()
cutoff_after_step = one_rule.cutoff.item()
print(grad_at_start, grad_after_backward, cutoff_after_step)
```

The code runs the first [training step](#def-training-step) of @sol-train-soft-rule one call at a time.
A new [parameter](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-parameter) has no stored gradient,
so its `.grad` is `None`.
After `loss.backward()`,
the cutoff's `.grad` holds the slope of $\emprisk$ at $\param = 0$,
`r sprintf("%.4f", py$grad_after_backward)`.
Then `optimizer.step()` moves the cutoff from 0 to
$0 - `r py$learning_rate` \times (`r sprintf("%.4f", py$grad_after_backward)`) = `r sprintf("%.4f", py$cutoff_after_step)`$.

:::
